From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a **list of Tanzanian Twenty20 International cricketers**.
In April 2018, the ICC decided to grant full Twenty20 International (T20I) status to all its members. Therefore, all Twenty20 matches played between Tanzania and other ICC members after 1 January 2019 are eligible to have full T20I status.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-1) Tanzania played their first T20I matches in November 2021 during the [2021 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_Qualifier#Group_B "2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier") in Kigali.
This list comprises all members of the Tanzania cricket team who have played at least one T20I match. It is initially arranged in the order in which each player won his first Twenty20 cap. Where more than one player won their first Twenty20 cap in the same match, their names are listed alphabetically by surname.
**General**

*   ‡ – Captain  
*   † – Wicket-keeper  
*   **First** – Year of debut  
*   **Last** – Year of latest game  
*   **Mat** – Number of matches played**Batting**

*   **Runs** – Runs scored in career  
*   **HS** – Highest score  
*   **Avg** – Runs scored per dismissal  
*   ***** – Batsman remained not out  
*   **50** – Half centuries scored  
*   **100** – Centuries scored**Bowling**

*   **Balls** – Balls bowled in career  
*   **Wkt** – Wickets taken in career  
*   **BBI** – Best bowling in an innings  
*   **Ave** – Average runs per wicket**Fielding**

*   **Ca** – Catches taken  
*   **St** – Stumpings affected  
_Statistics are correct as of 28 March 2026._[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-apps-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-4)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a **list of Tanzanian Twenty20 International cricketers**.
In April 2018, the ICC decided to grant full Twenty20 International (T20I) status to all its members. Therefore, all Twenty20 matches played between Tanzania and other ICC members after 1 January 2019 are eligible to have full T20I status.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-1) Tanzania played their first T20I matches in November 2021 during the [2021 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_Qualifier#Group_B "2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier") in Kigali.
This list comprises all members of the Tanzania cricket team who have played at least one T20I match. It is initially arranged in the order in which each player won his first Twenty20 cap. Where more than one player won their first Twenty20 cap in the same match, their names are listed alphabetically by surname.
**General**

*   † – Wicket-keeper

*   **Last** – Year of latest game

*   **100** – Centuries scored**Bowling**

*   **Balls** – Balls bowled in career  
*   **Wkt** – Wickets taken in career  
*   **BBI** – Best bowling in an innings  
*   **Ave** – Average runs per wicket**Fielding**

*   **Ca** – Catches taken  
*   **St** – Stumpings affected  
_Statistics are correct as of 28 March 2026._[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-apps-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Tanzania_Twenty20_International_cricketers#cite_note-4)

# 2007 Kenya Twenty20 Quadrangular
The **2007 Kenya Twenty20 Quadrangular** was a Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket tournament held in Kenya from 1 to 4 September 2007. The four participating teams were Bangladesh, Kenya, Pakistan and Uganda (matches involving Uganda were not classed as T20I matches as the team did not hold such status). The matches were all played at the Gymkhana Club Ground in Nairobi.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Kenya_Twenty20_Quadrangular#cite_note-series-1)
For Bangladesh, Kenya and Pakistan, this tournament was a warm-up for the inaugural ICC World Twenty20 that was to be held later in September.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Kenya_Twenty20_Quadrangular#cite_note-warmup-2)

# 2007 Kenya Twenty20 Quadrangular
The **2007 Kenya Twenty20 Quadrangular** was a Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket tournament held in Kenya from 1 to 4 September 2007. The four participating teams were Bangladesh, Kenya, Pakistan and Uganda (matches involving Uganda were not classed as T20I matches as the team did not hold such status). The matches were all played at the Gymkhana Club Ground in Nairobi.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Kenya_Twenty20_Quadrangular#cite_note-series-1)
For Bangladesh, Kenya and Pakistan, this tournament was a warm-up for the inaugural ICC World Twenty20 that was to be held later in September.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Kenya_Twenty20_Quadrangular#cite_note-warmup-2)

The **2004–05 ABN-AMRO Twenty-20 Cup** was the first edition of the ABN-AMRO Twenty-20 Cup, a domestic Twenty20 tournament in Pakistan sponsored by ABN AMRO bank. It was held from 25 to 30 April 2005 in Lahore. The Faisalabad Wolves won the tournament by defeating the Karachi Dolphins in the final.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-1) As the winners, the Faisalabad Wolves were invited to compete in the International 20:20 Club Championship, hosted by Leicestershire County Cricket Club in England, in September 2005, which they also won.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-2)
This was the first Twenty20 tournament in the country, after the introduction of the Twenty20 format in 2003. It was huge success with the final having an attendance of 30,000. It helped increase the popularity of cricket in Pakistan and became an annual tournament.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-prize-4)

The tournament also involved a match-throwing incident with Sialkot Stallions captain Shoaib Malik.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-5)
The eleven teams are divided into three groups: Groups A and B with four teams each and Group C with three. Each team plays a single round-robin tournament and the top team from each group, determined by a point system, advances to the triangular series. The triangular series is another round-robin tournament where the top two teams advance to the final.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-points-6)

The winners are awarded a trophy and Rs. 300,000 while the runners-up receive Rs. 150,000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-prize-4)

## Match-throwing incident
[edit]
The tournament involved a match-throwing incident in the match between the Sialkot Stallions and the Karachi Zebras. Shoaib Malik, the captain of the Stallions, openly admitted to deliberately losing their match against the Karachi Zebras in an attempt to eliminate the Lahore Eagles from the competition. Neither team received points for the match. PCB declared the match void and Karachi Zebras were denied a place in the triangular phase of the ABN Amro Twenty20 Cup despite winning their Pool 'B' fixture against Sialkot Stallions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-7) Malik was expressing his disappointment at earlier decisions in the competition that he felt went against his side and it did not involve any match-fixing or financial implications.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-8)
Malik's actions were against his code of conduct as a Test cricketer and had effect on the image of Pakistan cricket, the sponsors and the audience. After realising this, Malik later apologised. He was banned for one Test match and fined Rs. 10,000 and 75% of his match fees for two One Day International matches.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-malik-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-10)

The **2004–05 ABN-AMRO Twenty-20 Cup** was the first edition of the ABN-AMRO Twenty-20 Cup, a domestic Twenty20 tournament in Pakistan sponsored by ABN AMRO bank. It was held from 25 to 30 April 2005 in Lahore. The Faisalabad Wolves won the tournament by defeating the Karachi Dolphins in the final.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-1) As the winners, the Faisalabad Wolves were invited to compete in the International 20:20 Club Championship, hosted by Leicestershire County Cricket Club in England, in September 2005, which they also won.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-2)
This was the first Twenty20 tournament in the country, after the introduction of the Twenty20 format in 2003. It was huge success with the final having an attendance of 30,000. It helped increase the popularity of cricket in Pakistan and became an annual tournament.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-prize-4)
texts.1:
The tournament also involved a match-throwing incident with Sialkot Stallions captain Shoaib Malik.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-5)
The eleven teams are divided into three groups: Groups A and B with four teams each and Group C with three. Each team plays a single round-robin tournament and the top team from each group, determined by a point system, advances to the triangular series. The triangular series is another round-robin tournament where the top two teams advance to the final.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-points-6)

## Match-throwing incident
[edit]
The tournament involved a match-throwing incident in the match between the Sialkot Stallions and the Karachi Zebras. Shoaib Malik, the captain of the Stallions, openly admitted to deliberately losing their match against the Karachi Zebras in an attempt to eliminate the Lahore Eagles from the competition. Neither team received points for the match. PCB declared the match void and Karachi Zebras were denied a place in the triangular phase of the ABN Amro Twenty20 Cup despite winning their Pool 'B' fixture against Sialkot Stallions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-7) Malik was expressing his disappointment at earlier decisions in the competition that he felt went against his side and it did not involve any match-fixing or financial implications.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-8)
Malik's actions were against his code of conduct as a Test cricketer and had effect on the image of Pakistan cricket, the sponsors and the audience. After realising this, Malik later apologised. He was banned for one Test match and fined Rs. 10,000 and 75% of his match fees for two One Day International matches.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-malik-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_National_Twenty20_Cup#cite_note-10)

On 6 April 2013, ICC unveiled the logo of the tournament at a gala event in Dhaka. The overall look of the logo design is primarily inspired by the unique Bangladesh decoration art style. The logo uses the colours of the Bangladeshi flag with splashes of blue representing the country's rivers (also as being the ICC's own colour). The logo is also inspired by the rickshaws.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Cricket.com.pk-35) The T is made up of cricket stumps and the '0' in the T20 represents the cricket ball complete with a green seam.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-37)

## Team of the tournament
_**Char Chokka Hoi Hoi**_ (Bengali: চার ছক্কা হৈ হৈ; English: Fours, Sixes, Fun and Games)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Malaysia_Sun-38) was the official theme song of the 2014 ICC World Twenty20.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Zeenews-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Cricketcounty-40) It was released worldwide on 20 February 2014. Most of the song is in Bengali while some phrases in the opening lines are in English. The song is composed by famous Bangladeshi composer and artist Fuad al Muqtadir and has been sung by an ensemble of young vocalists, namely Dilshad Nahar Kona, Elita Karim, Pantha Kanai, Johan Alamgir, Sanvir Huda, Badhon Sarkar Puja and Kaushik Hossain Taposh.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Malaysia_Sun-38) The song is notable for its playful use of "Banglish".

On 6 April 2013, ICC unveiled the logo of the tournament at a gala event in Dhaka. The overall look of the logo design is primarily inspired by the unique Bangladesh decoration art style. The logo uses the colours of the Bangladeshi flag with splashes of blue representing the country's rivers (also as being the ICC's own colour). The logo is also inspired by the rickshaws.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Cricket.com.pk-35) The T is made up of cricket stumps and the '0' in the T20 represents the cricket ball complete with a green seam.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-37)

## Team of the tournament
_**Char Chokka Hoi Hoi**_ (Bengali: চার ছক্কা হৈ হৈ; English: Fours, Sixes, Fun and Games)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Malaysia_Sun-38) was the official theme song of the 2014 ICC World Twenty20.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Zeenews-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Cricketcounty-40) It was released worldwide on 20 February 2014. Most of the song is in Bengali while some phrases in the opening lines are in English. The song is composed by famous Bangladeshi composer and artist Fuad al Muqtadir and has been sung by an ensemble of young vocalists, namely Dilshad Nahar Kona, Elita Karim, Pantha Kanai, Johan Alamgir, Sanvir Huda, Badhon Sarkar Puja and Kaushik Hossain Taposh.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Twenty20#cite_note-Malaysia_Sun-38) The song is notable for its playful use of "Banglish".

The **Namibia women's national cricket team**, nicknamed the **Capricorn Eagles**,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-4) represents Namibia in international [women's cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_cricket "Women's cricket"). The team is organised by Cricket Namibia, which has been a member of the International Cricket Council (ICC) since 1992.

Namibia made its international debut at the 2004 [ICC Africa Women's Twenty20 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Africa_Women's_Twenty20_Championship "ICC Africa Women's Twenty20 Championship") in Tanzania, but failed to win a match.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-mat-5) The team's closest result came in the opening match against [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_women's_national_cricket_team "Kenya women's national cricket team"), where they were bowled out for 106, and eventually lost by five wickets.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-6) In the second game, against [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda_women's_national_cricket_team "Uganda women's national cricket team"), they lost by 152 runs,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-7) while in the final game, against [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_women's_national_cricket_team "Tanzania women's national cricket team"), they were bowled out for just 29, and lost by ten wickets.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-8) After their debut, Namibia did not compete in another Africa-wide tournament until the 2011 [ICC Africa Women's Twenty20 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICC_Africa_Women's_Twenty20_Championship "ICC Africa Women's Twenty20 Championship") in Uganda. They have since regularly competed in ICC Africa competitions, without much success.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-mat-5) Namibia also play in regional competitions against other southern African teams, and in the past have appeared in South African provincial competitions (as the national men's team does).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-9)

In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full [Women's Twenty20 International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_Twenty20_International "Women's Twenty20 International") (WT20I) status to all its members. Therefore, all Twenty20 matches played between Namibia women and other ICC members since 1 July 2018 have the full WT20I status.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-10)

Namibia's first WT20I matches were contested as part of the [Botswana 7s tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Botswana_Cricket_Association_Women's_T20I_Series "2018 Botswana Cricket Association Women's T20I Series") in August 2018 against [Botswana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botswana_women's_national_cricket_team "Botswana women's national cricket team"), [Lesotho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesotho_women's_national_cricket_team "Lesotho women's national cricket team"), [Malawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malawi_women's_national_cricket_team "Malawi women's national cricket team"), [Mozambique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mozambique_women's_national_cricket_team "Mozambique women's national cricket team"), [Sierra Leone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Leone_women's_national_cricket_team "Sierra Leone women's national cricket team") and [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia_women's_national_cricket_team "Zambia women's national cricket team") (Zambia's matches were not classified as WT20Is as they had a Botswanan player in their squad).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-11) Namibia finished top of the table, winning all five group stage matches[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-12) and won the final against Sierra Leone by a margin of nine wickets.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-14)

In July 2019, the International Cricket Council (ICC) suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-16) The following month, with Zimbabwe banned from taking part in international cricket tournaments, the ICC confirmed that Namibia would replace them in the [2019 ICC Women's World Twenty20 Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_Women's_World_Twenty20_Qualifier "2019 ICC Women's World Twenty20 Qualifier") tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-Namibia-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-18)
In December 2020, the ICC announced the qualification pathway for the [2023 ICC Women's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ICC_Women's_T20_World_Cup "2023 ICC Women's T20 World Cup").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-19) Namibia were named in the [2021 ICC Women's T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_Women's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_Qualifier "2021 ICC Women's T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier") regional group, alongside ten other teams.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-20)

In March 2024, Cricket Namibia awarded professional contracts to members of the women's team for the first time, with 10 players receiving a contract.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-21) As a result, Cricket Namibia became the first sporting body in Namibia to award central contracts to both men and women.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-22)

In July 2019, the International Cricket Council (ICC) suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-16) The following month, with Zimbabwe banned from taking part in international cricket tournaments, the ICC confirmed that Namibia would replace them in the [2019 ICC Women's World Twenty20 Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_ICC_Women's_World_Twenty20_Qualifier "2019 ICC Women's World Twenty20 Qualifier") tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-Namibia-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-18)
In December 2020, the ICC announced the qualification pathway for the [2023 ICC Women's T20 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ICC_Women's_T20_World_Cup "2023 ICC Women's T20 World Cup").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-19) Namibia were named in the [2021 ICC Women's T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ICC_Women's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_Qualifier "2021 ICC Women's T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier") regional group, alongside ten other teams.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-20)
texts.7: In March 2024, Cricket Namibia awarded professional contracts to members of the women's team for the first time, with 10 players receiving a contract.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-21) As a result, Cricket Namibia became the first sporting body in Namibia to award central contracts to both men and women.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namibia_women's_national_cricket_team#cite_note-22)

3,428 What a sensational knock from Rwanda’s star as Fanny Utagushimaninde delivers a stunning 111 runs off just 65 balls on her senior national team debut. Rwanda Women post a massive 210/3 in 20 overs against Ghana 💥 It’s now game on as Ghana chase 211 for victory. Can they do it? 👀 #RwandaCricket #CricketRwanda #WomensCricket #T20Cricket #GameOn RwandaVsGhana
820K A journey to be proud of and memories to last a lifetime for Tanzania’s rising stars 🫶 Follow #U19WorldCup LIVE, broadcast details in our bio 📺
632 https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/rwanda-s-fanny-utagushimaninde-becomes-youngest-centurion-in-women-s-t20is-1528515
638 Ahead of the ICC U19 Women’s T20 World Cup Africa Division 2 Qualifier in Uganda, our captain shares her thoughts on the team’s preparation and mindset going into the tournament. Focused. United. Ready to represent Malawi. The journey begins now. 📺 Watch the matches live via: https://www.youtube.com/@cricketuganda 👉 Like, follow, and watch this space for match updates, fixtures and highlights of Cricket Malawi Action. Join our WhatsApp Channel for more: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb6VrW6IXnljwScFnr1w #MalawiWomen #U19WomensCricket #RoadToWorldCup #StriveForExcellence ICC Africa Cricket School of Excellence Cricket Uganda @africa.icc @cricketschoolofexcellence @cricketuganda
910 Just one day to go. #U19WT20AQDiv2

926 ​PLAY OF THE DAY! 🌟🏏 ​History has been made in Lagos! On her T20I debut, Rwanda’s Fanny Uwagushimaninde has produced a magical century at the #NCFInvitational2026. 🇷🇼✨ ​To score a hundred is a feat—to do it on your international debut is legendary. We salute Fanny as she joins the elite ranks of players to reach triple figures in their very first appearance! 💯🙌 ​A star is born! ⭐️ ​#PlayOfTheDay #RwandaCricket #NCFInvitational #WomensCricket
2,726 Coach Kyle shares his thoughts as the team prepares for the ICC U19 Women’s T20 World Cup Africa Division 2 Qualifier in Uganda. Preparation has been focused. Standards have been high. The group is ready for the challenge ahead. Representing Malawi with pride 🇲🇼 📺 Watch the matches live via: https://www.youtube.com/@cricketuganda 👉 Like, follow, and watch this space for match updates, fixtures and highlights of Cricket Malawi Action. Join our WhatsApp Channel for more: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb6VrW6IXnljwScFnr1w #MalawiWomen #U19WomensCricket #RoadToWorldCup #StriveForExcellence @cricketuganda Cricket Uganda @cricketschoolofexcellence Cricket School of Excellence ICC Africa @africa.icc @durant__kyle
242 Pressure. Precision. Composure. Rwanda defend 104 in 14 overs to edge South Africa U19 by just 4 runs in a gripping finish. Sealed by the DLS method. #nigeriacricketfederation #Nigeriawomeninvitational2026
2,722 Historic Century for 15-Year-Old Rwandan Cricketer. At just 15 years old, Rwandan cricketer Utagushimaninde has made history by becoming the first woman to score a century on her T20I debut. A truly remarkable achievement making headlines around the world. What a moment for her and Rwandan cricket! 🇷🇼🏏 #cricket #t20i #t20 #rwanda #icc

5,682 15 years old. T20I debut. A century. 🤯 Rwanda’s Fanny Utagushimaninde smashes 111* off 65, becoming the first-ever to score a hundred on women’s T20I debut 🔥 Youngest centurion in the T20I format ✔️ Record-breaking knock ✔️ Player of the Match ✔️ She’s not just arrived, she’s made history. ✨ . . . . #FannyUtagushimaninde #Cricket #WomensCricket #Rwanda #OnThisDay
1,765 Our Women’s National Team has officially landed safely in Nigeria after departing from Rwanda today. The journey to the Nigeria Women’s Invitational T20I begins now. We wish our girls the very best as they represent the nation with pride 🇷🇼❤️ #RwandaCricket #GrowingWithEveryStep
498K A four-wicket haul and a half-century 👏 Don’t miss the @aramco POTM Highlights of Nihar Parmar’s all-round heroics for Japan against Tanzania in the #U19WorldCup 🎥

Title: 2018–19 Men's T20 World Cup Africa qualifier
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The **2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier** was a tournament played as part of qualification process for the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-1)
Twelve regional qualifiers for the 2021 World Cup were held by the International Cricket Council (ICC), with 62 teams[[n 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Teams-2) competing during 2018 in five regions – Africa (3 groups), Americas (2), Asia (2), East Asia Pacific (2) and Europe (3). The top 25 sides from these progressed to five Regional Finals in 2019, with seven teams then going on to compete in the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)[[n 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-UAE=sr-4) along with the six lowest ranked sides from the ICC T20I Championship.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)

The first African sub-regional qualifier (North-Western sub region) was held in Nigeria, with the two other groups staged in Botswana and Rwanda.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Road_to_2020-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Africa_sub_region-6) The top two teams in each group advanced to the regional finals tournament, which will determine two African entrants to the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier. In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full international status to Twenty20 men's matches played between member sides from 1 January 2019 onwards. Therefore, all the matches in the Regional Finals were played as Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-status-7)

From the North-Western sub region group, both Ghana and Nigeria qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-GhaNgr-8)Simon Ateak of Ghana was named the player of the tournament in the North-Western group.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-9) The second group, the Eastern sub region, started on 7 July 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-10) Both Kenya and Uganda qualified for the Africa Regional Finals from the Eastern sub region group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Kenya-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uganda-12) Uganda's Riazat Ali Shah was named the player of the tournament for the Eastern group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-RAS-13) From the Southern sub region group, Botswana and Namibia qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-BotNam-14)

The Regional Finals were held in Uganda in May 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uga19-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-16) Namibia and Kenya both progressed to the T20 World Cup Qualifier after finishing first and second respectively in the Regional Finals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-17) In July 2019, the ICC suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-18) As a result of their suspension, the ICC confirmed that Nigeria would replace them in the T20 World Cup Qualifier tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-19)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The **2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier** was a tournament played as part of qualification process for the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-1)
Twelve regional qualifiers for the 2021 World Cup were held by the International Cricket Council (ICC), with 62 teams[[n 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Teams-2) competing during 2018 in five regions – Africa (3 groups), Americas (2), Asia (2), East Asia Pacific (2) and Europe (3). The top 25 sides from these progressed to five Regional Finals in 2019, with seven teams then going on to compete in the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)[[n 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-UAE=sr-4) along with the six lowest ranked sides from the ICC T20I Championship.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)
texts.1: The first African sub-regional qualifier (North-Western sub region) was held in Nigeria, with the two other groups staged in Botswana and Rwanda.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Road_to_2020-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Africa_sub_region-6) The top two teams in each group advanced to the regional finals tournament, which will determine two African entrants to the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier. In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full international status to Twenty20 men's matches played between member sides from 1 January 2019 onwards. Therefore, all the matches in the Regional Finals were played as Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-status-7)
texts.2: From the North-Western sub region group, both Ghana and Nigeria qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-GhaNgr-8)Simon Ateak of Ghana was named the player of the tournament in the North-Western group.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-9) The second group, the Eastern sub region, started on 7 July 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-10) Both Kenya and Uganda qualified for the Africa Regional Finals from the Eastern sub region group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Kenya-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uganda-12) Uganda's Riazat Ali Shah was named the player of the tournament for the Eastern group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-RAS-13) From the Southern sub region group, Botswana and Namibia qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-BotNam-14)

The Regional Finals were held in Uganda in May 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uga19-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-16) Namibia and Kenya both progressed to the T20 World Cup Qualifier after finishing first and second respectively in the Regional Finals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-17) In July 2019, the ICC suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-18) As a result of their suspension, the ICC confirmed that Nigeria would replace them in the T20 World Cup Qualifier tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-19)

Just three days after the Black Stars pipped the Super Eagles to the Qatar 2022 ticket, the two countries go head-to-head in women’s cricket in Lagos.

# Nigeria, Ghana in epic semi-final duel at Women T20I
## Nigeria has had a smooth run so far in the competition with clear wins over The Gambia and Sierra Leone women’s teams.
### Join the Premium Times WhatsApp Community For Quick Access To News and Happenings Around You.Open in WhatsApp
With two victories in the bag, the Nigeria women’s cricket team will resume the Women’s T20I Invitational Cricket title chase on Friday, April 1, 2022, with an all-important duel against Ghana’s Women’s Cricket team.
The Ghanaian Women, locked down their first win on Wednesday running roughshod over the Gambia with a 104-run blowout.
Their first two matches with Rwanda and Sierra Leone earlier in the week had left them with defeats.
|  |  |  
| --- | --- |
Nigeria has however had a smooth run so far with clean shoves of the Gambia and Sierra Leone Women’s teams to pitch them as favourites along with Rwanda for the title in the five-nation invitational.
The encounter with Ghanaian women, apart from stoking the traditional rivalry, will also test Nigeria’s stability and hunger to give the title a chase, before their finals test against Rwanda on Saturday.
The hosts are ranked 37th by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)**, albeit Ghana is yet to be ranked by the world cricket governing body.

# Nigeria, Ghana in epic semi-final duel at Women T20I

Add as a preferred source on Google
Both teams had met earlier at a Women’s Invitational in Ghana in 2018, with Nigeria gaining the upper hand by a four-run win.
The Ghanian Women’s team, led by Rhyda Ofori, has a number of its players drawn from a recently concluded Ashanti Region T20 tournament.
The team also played against an Under 19 selected side as part of preparations for this event.
Ofori’s side should however be wary of Nigeria’s captain Blessing Etim, who was player-of-the-match with bowling statistics of two wickets, 16 runs in four overs against Sierra Leone.
Also, teammate Salome Sunday, who got the tournament’s first half-century in the same game will be a handful.
Another player of note is medium-pace bowler, 15-year-old Lilian Ude, whose bowling ability earned her a debut in the team as she showed good class to become Player of the Match in the team’s second game against the Gambia.
Ude’s two overs, two wickets, and two maidens earned her that individual award in her second cap for the national team.
The hosts should also show respect to her unranked opponents especially the likes of Felicia Serwaa and Elizabeth Annor with the best batting performances in the game against the Gambia, as well as bowler Janet.
Fans will be hoping to get consolation from this game, having seen the Super Eagles lose the Qatar 2022 World Cup ticket to Ghana a few days ago.
Whichever the situation, the game promises to be a cracker at the ten-strip Tafawa Balewa Square Cricket Oval in Lagos.

texts.56:
# Nigeria, Ghana in epic semi-final duel at Women T20I
## Nigeria has had a smooth run so far in the competition with clear wins over The Gambia and Sierra Leone women’s teams.
### Join the Premium Times WhatsApp Community For Quick Access To News and Happenings Around You.Open in WhatsApp
With two victories in the bag, the Nigeria women’s cricket team will resume the Women’s T20I Invitational Cricket title chase on Friday, April 1, 2022, with an all-important duel against Ghana’s Women’s Cricket team.
The Ghanaian Women, locked down their first win on Wednesday running roughshod over the Gambia with a 104-run blowout.
Their first two matches with Rwanda and Sierra Leone earlier in the week had left them with defeats.
|  |  |  
| --- | --- |
Nigeria has however had a smooth run so far with clean shoves of the Gambia and Sierra Leone Women’s teams to pitch them as favourites along with Rwanda for the title in the five-nation invitational.
The encounter with Ghanaian women, apart from stoking the traditional rivalry, will also test Nigeria’s stability and hunger to give the title a chase, before their finals test against Rwanda on Saturday.
The hosts are ranked 37th by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)**, albeit Ghana is yet to be ranked by the world cricket governing body.
texts.57:
# Nigeria, Ghana in epic semi-final duel at Women T20I
## Stay Ahead with Premium Times
Follow us on Google News and never miss breaking stories, investigations, and in-depth reporting.
Add as a preferred source on Google
Both teams had met earlier at a Women’s Invitational in Ghana in 2018, with Nigeria gaining the upper hand by a four-run win.
The Ghanian Women’s team, led by Rhyda Ofori, has a number of its players drawn from a recently concluded Ashanti Region T20 tournament.
The team also played against an Under 19 selected side as part of preparations for this event.
Ofori’s side should however be wary of Nigeria’s captain Blessing Etim, who was player-of-the-match with bowling statistics of two wickets, 16 runs in four overs against Sierra Leone.
Also, teammate Salome Sunday, who got the tournament’s first half-century in the same game will be a handful.
Another player of note is medium-pace bowler, 15-year-old Lilian Ude, whose bowling ability earned her a debut in the team as she showed good class to become Player of the Match in the team’s second game against the Gambia.
Ude’s two overs, two wickets, and two maidens earned her that individual award in her second cap for the national team.
The hosts should also show respect to her unranked opponents especially the likes of Felicia Serwaa and Elizabeth Annor with the best batting performances in the game against the Gambia, as well as bowler Janet.
Fans will be hoping to get consolation from this game, having seen the Super Eagles lose the Qatar 2022 World Cup ticket to Ghana a few days ago.
Whichever the situation, the game promises to be a cracker at the ten-strip Tafawa Balewa Square Cricket Oval in Lagos.

Title: 2018–19 Men's T20 World Cup Africa qualifier

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The **2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier** was a tournament played as part of qualification process for the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-1)
Twelve regional qualifiers for the 2021 World Cup were held by the International Cricket Council (ICC), with 62 teams[[n 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Teams-2) competing during 2018 in five regions – Africa (3 groups), Americas (2), Asia (2), East Asia Pacific (2) and Europe (3). The top 25 sides from these progressed to five Regional Finals in 2019, with seven teams then going on to compete in the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)[[n 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-UAE=sr-4) along with the six lowest ranked sides from the ICC T20I Championship.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)

The first African sub-regional qualifier (North-Western sub region) was held in Nigeria, with the two other groups staged in Botswana and Rwanda.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Road_to_2020-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Africa_sub_region-6) The top two teams in each group advanced to the regional finals tournament, which will determine two African entrants to the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier. In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full international status to Twenty20 men's matches played between member sides from 1 January 2019 onwards. Therefore, all the matches in the Regional Finals were played as Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-status-7)

From the North-Western sub region group, both Ghana and Nigeria qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-GhaNgr-8)Simon Ateak of Ghana was named the player of the tournament in the North-Western group.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-9) The second group, the Eastern sub region, started on 7 July 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-10) Both Kenya and Uganda qualified for the Africa Regional Finals from the Eastern sub region group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Kenya-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uganda-12) Uganda's Riazat Ali Shah was named the player of the tournament for the Eastern group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-RAS-13) From the Southern sub region group, Botswana and Namibia qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-BotNam-14)

The Regional Finals were held in Uganda in May 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uga19-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-16) Namibia and Kenya both progressed to the T20 World Cup Qualifier after finishing first and second respectively in the Regional Finals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-17) In July 2019, the ICC suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-18) As a result of their suspension, the ICC confirmed that Nigeria would replace them in the T20 World Cup Qualifier tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-19)

# Nigeria and Ghana continue dominance in Africa World T20 Qualifiers
16 April, 2018
*   _Ademola Onikoyi smashes 75 off 55 deliveries_  
*   _Simon Ateak player of the match with half century_  
*   _Sierra Leone and The Gambia hope to get off the mark_
Nigeria continued their fine form on day two of the ICC World T20 Africa Qualifier A, as they saw off The Gambia by 55 runs, at the Tafawa Balewa Square Cricket Oval in Lagos on Sunday.
The Nigerians again batted first, and they piled on the runs, eventually notching a formidable 176 for five in their 20 overs. The star for the home side was Ademola Onikoyi, who blazed an undefeated 75 off just 55 balls. There were two massive sixes and nine fours in the free-spirited knock, as the number three took Nigeria to a place of comfort. Skipper Chimezie Onwuzulike continued his fine form, with a quick-fire 34 off just 18 balls.

The total was always going to be a massive test for The Gambia, who had lost their opening match to Ghana by 58 runs. They again breached the 100 mark, thanks in main to a belligerent knock of 29 off just 16 balls by PA Hassan Faye. He struck three sixes for good measure.

# Nigeria and Ghana continue dominance in Africa World T20 Qualifiers
Nigeria sit top of the standings, but they are joined by their neighbours, Ghana, who also made it two from two matches on Sunday. The Black Sticks were pushed by Sierra Leone, after they to batted first and racked up a total of 140 for eight. Simon Ateak was the mainstay, striking a composed 57 off 42 balls.
In response, Sierra Leone were feisty, but the required rate of seven an over proved beyond their developing top-order. Lansana Lamin kept them interested with 28 off 25 deliveries, but he needed help from the other end.
Ultimately, Ghana prevailed by 31 runs, but the fact that Sierra Leone made it beyond 100 was due to some ill-discipline with the ball, which saw 13 extras conceded – including nine wides. Ghana will want to iron out some of those frailties ahead of their clash against Nigeria, as those two will clearly battle it out for bragging rights this week.
The action resumes tomorrow with Sierra Leone and The Gambia in the morning, followed by the Yellow Greens and Black Sticks in the afternoon.

# Nigeria and Ghana continue dominance in Africa World T20 Qualifiers
16 April, 2018
*   _Ademola Onikoyi smashes 75 off 55 deliveries_  
*   _Simon Ateak player of the match with half century_  
*   _Sierra Leone and The Gambia hope to get off the mark_
Nigeria continued their fine form on day two of the ICC World T20 Africa Qualifier A, as they saw off The Gambia by 55 runs, at the Tafawa Balewa Square Cricket Oval in Lagos on Sunday.
The Nigerians again batted first, and they piled on the runs, eventually notching a formidable 176 for five in their 20 overs. The star for the home side was Ademola Onikoyi, who blazed an undefeated 75 off just 55 balls. There were two massive sixes and nine fours in the free-spirited knock, as the number three took Nigeria to a place of comfort. Skipper Chimezie Onwuzulike continued his fine form, with a quick-fire 34 off just 18 balls.

# Nigeria and Ghana continue dominance in Africa World T20 Qualifiers
Nigeria sit top of the standings, but they are joined by their neighbours, Ghana, who also made it two from two matches on Sunday. The Black Sticks were pushed by Sierra Leone, after they to batted first and racked up a total of 140 for eight. Simon Ateak was the mainstay, striking a composed 57 off 42 balls.
In response, Sierra Leone were feisty, but the required rate of seven an over proved beyond their developing top-order. Lansana Lamin kept them interested with 28 off 25 deliveries, but he needed help from the other end.
Ultimately, Ghana prevailed by 31 runs, but the fact that Sierra Leone made it beyond 100 was due to some ill-discipline with the ball, which saw 13 extras conceded – including nine wides. Ghana will want to iron out some of those frailties ahead of their clash against Nigeria, as those two will clearly battle it out for bragging rights this week.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The **2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier** was a tournament played as part of qualification process for the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-1)
Twelve regional qualifiers for the 2021 World Cup were held by the International Cricket Council (ICC), with 62 teams[[n 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Teams-2) competing during 2018 in five regions – Africa (3 groups), Americas (2), Asia (2), East Asia Pacific (2) and Europe (3). The top 25 sides from these progressed to five Regional Finals in 2019, with seven teams then going on to compete in the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)[[n 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-UAE=sr-4) along with the six lowest ranked sides from the ICC T20I Championship.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)
texts.1: The first African sub-regional qualifier (North-Western sub region) was held in Nigeria, with the two other groups staged in Botswana and Rwanda.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Road_to_2020-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Africa_sub_region-6) The top two teams in each group advanced to the regional finals tournament, which will determine two African entrants to the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier. In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full international status to Twenty20 men's matches played between member sides from 1 January 2019 onwards. Therefore, all the matches in the Regional Finals were played as Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-status-7)
texts.2: From the North-Western sub region group, both Ghana and Nigeria qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-GhaNgr-8)Simon Ateak of Ghana was named the player of the tournament in the North-Western group.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-9) The second group, the Eastern sub region, started on 7 July 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-10) Both Kenya and Uganda qualified for the Africa Regional Finals from the Eastern sub region group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Kenya-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uganda-12) Uganda's Riazat Ali Shah was named the player of the tournament for the Eastern group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-RAS-13) From the Southern sub region group, Botswana and Namibia qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-BotNam-14)
texts.3:
The Regional Finals were held in Uganda in May 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uga19-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-16) Namibia and Kenya both progressed to the T20 World Cup Qualifier after finishing first and second respectively in the Regional Finals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-17) In July 2019, the ICC suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-18) As a result of their suspension, the ICC confirmed that Nigeria would replace them in the T20 World Cup Qualifier tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-19)
